To: Operations, Sales, and Finance Leadership
From: Supply Chain Director
Date: [Insert Date]
Subject: Cost-Effective Shipping Plan Across Our Multi-Node Network

Situation:
We are distributing products from multiple warehouses, plants, and distribution centers to a broad network of stores, customers, and regional hubs. Service expectations are high, and freight costs vary significantly by route. Partial shipments are allowed, so orders can be split and shipped in the quantities that make the most sense operationally and financially.

Problem:
We need a clear, data-driven shipping plan that determines how much to ship from each source to each destination so that:
- We do not exceed available inventory or shipping capacity at any source.
- Every destination receives its required quantity on time.
- Total shipping spend is kept as low as possible by selecting the most economical routes.

This effort matters because it directly affects our freight spend, inventory utilization, and customer satisfaction. The attached data includes available inventory by source, required quantities by destination, and per-route shipping costs. Using this information, we will evaluate the full set of feasible routing options and allocate volumes to cost-advantaged lanes while honoring all supply and demand requirements. The outcome will be a practical, lane-level plan that can be executed by transportation and warehouse teams, along with visibility to expected freight spend and source utilization. We will also review the plan for operational practicality (e.g., consolidations, service levels, and handling considerations) before execution.
